newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Jan-June foreign investment rises on 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chile Jan-June foreign investment rises on 1996.

text.p: Fresh foreign investment in Chile rose to $3.6 billion in the first six months of the year, up 33 percent on the same period last year, said Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia.
Direct investment in projects through Decree Law 600 totalled $2 billion, with investment through the sale of Chilean American Depositary Receipts at $1.3 billion, he told a news conference.
Investment under the central bank's Chapter 19 rules allowing fresh capital transfers to existing projects totalled $208 million.
Investment via ADRs climbed 93 percent on last year, while direct investment rose by a moderate 10 percent in the first six months of the year.
The government's foreign investment committee authorized investment totalling $4.2 billion in the first half of this year, said Garcia.
The figure was boosted by the authorization in May of a $2.75 billion investment in the huge Los Pelambres copper mine being built by a Chilean/Japanese consortium.
The Los Pelambres investment will be channeled through a British company and two Dutch-registered firms.
